User Story: As a security owner I want TLS, the body cap and identity injection to happen at an edge the application can trust, with client-supplied identity headers stripped before they reach it.

Feature Name: AI security review of pull requests
User Story: As a maintainer I want each PR diff reviewed for security issues, without the reviewer itself becoming an attack surface.
Expected Behaviour: security-review.yml runs anthropics/claude-code-security-review on pull_request, pinned to a commit SHA because no upstream tags exist. It self-skips until the CLAUDE_API_KEY repo secret exists, so PRs show no failing check before activation. The header records the activation steps and the residual risk explicitly: the action is not hardened against prompt injection, so it must only run on trusted diffs, and the recommended protected Environment with required reviewers is not enforceable from the workflow file.
Edge Cases: Secret absent (step self-skips); a fork PR (same-repo condition keeps it away from the secret); a compromised contributor or a misconfigured approval policy (documented as NOT mitigated).
Test Cases: Not runnable here - needs a GitHub PR and the CLAUDE_API_KEY secret
Notes: Reviewed as configuration only. The workflow is honest about its own threat model: the diff under review is attacker-controlled text handed to an agent holding an API key and write access, which is why the same-repo condition and the recommended protected Environment both exist. Whether CLAUDE_API_KEY is set is not visible from here.
